newsitem.title: USA: Vodafone CEO sees 20 pct earns rise in FY98.
newsitem.headline: Vodafone CEO sees 20 pct earns rise in FY98.

text.p: Vodafone Group Plc chief executive Chris Gent on Thursday predicted the British mobile telephone company's pre-tax earnings would grow close to 20 percent in the 1998 fiscal year.
Gent told Reuters he was "not uncomfortable" with analysts' projections for pre-tax earnings in fiscal 1997 and 1998. Those fiscal years end in March.
Gent, who spoke after a breakfast meeting with U.S. investors, said the company foresaw pre-tax earnings with "close to a 20 percent growth in 1997-98."
He would not detail figures. However, he described projections by NatWest Securities, which sponsored the meeting, as within a consensus range for 1997 and 1998 pre-tax earnings.

NatWest has estimated pre-tax income at 518 million pounds in fiscal 1997 and 623 million pounds in fiscal 1998. Pre-tax profits for the first half of the year were 252.4 million pounds, up 21 percent from the same period the year before.
"What we're looking at from the analysts don't make us uncomfortable," Gent said, adding of the projected 1998 figure, "Most people have us at 610."
Vodafone shares have risen in recent days, boosted in part by strong subscriber numbers in Britain. The company's American Depositary Receipt was up 1/8 to 45-1/8 in mid-morning New York trade.
Gent said Vodafone was not seeking a "strategic partner" or merger with regular telephone company. Market rumors in November had said AT&T Corp might bid for Vodafone, and Vodafone denied the rumors.
"We have a $12 billion market capitalization now, and you'd have to have a premium of 30 percent" to carry out a merger, he said.
"You look around the world, and who can swallow us? Very few."
A merger with the United States' AirTouch Communications Inc, for example, "would make investment bankers happy for a few weeks, but I don't know how good it would be for our shareholders."
